payload.prfaq:
PRESS RELEASE. quackitect's tool lane stops being the slow way to work. The agent now reads any file in parts, searches the working tree with real context and globs through ripgrep, searches the RECORD across shipped iterations and v1 through git refs, and changes six call sites in one atomic call. The rules that bind a step arrive with the step: a law minted this afternoon binds a session tomorrow, because applicable guidance is joined onto the packet instead of waiting to be discovered. And the gates stop asking the agent to vouch for its own conformance - what can be computed is computed, so a self-blessed killer rests on a lint's verdict rather than on the agent's attention. The owner keeps the involvement slider wherever they want it, including zero, and still owns the output - which is exactly why the machine, not the agent's prose, has to carry the mechanical half.

HOSTILE FAQ.

Q: You spent a day building tools instead of product. Isn't this yak-shaving?
A: The day this replaces cost three hand-rolled workarounds, three re-derivations of rulings the design document already contained, three release-gate rounds and one wrong conclusion from a confidently wrong search. The measurement is in the log, not in the feeling: se_file_patch is the most-used product tool at 645 calls AND the most-failing at 28, and it applies one edit per call.

Q: You are adding a dependency to a zero-dependency project, and deleting the fallback. What happens on a platform without a binary?
A: Search ceases - not degrades. That is the owner's explicit ruling and it is recorded as an accepted assumption (se.raid-rg-is-a-hard-dependency-with-no-fallback) with its own trigger and a fallback that is a documented manual install, not a resurrected second searcher. The assumption is about the user base, not the code, and it is true today.

Q: More lints means more ways for the machine to say no. Are you not about to make the lane slower in the name of making it faster?
A: This is the iteration's central risk and it has its own entry. The answer is a design constraint, not optimism: prefer lints that compute a FACT the evidence must match over lints that judge INTENT, because the first kind cannot be wrong about a correct build. And a lint that fires wrongly is a defect to remove, never a cost to absorb.

Q: What stops a lint from blocking an unattended run at 3am?
A: A ruled property - a lint DECIDES or DEFERS, never parks. Deferring means the check stays as prose exactly as today. That is the honest floor and it costs nothing.

Q: If every applicable rule is joined into every packet, will the agent not just skim a wall of law?
A: Yes, if relevance is not the mechanism. That failure is silent - nothing refuses, the rules are technically present, and they stop being read. The counter is narrow applies_to plus a MEASURED guidance size per packet, so the cost is visible rather than assumed harmless.

Q: You claim the record is searchable, but you also just discovered a closed iteration has a BRANCH and a TAG with the same name, which git calls ambiguous. Does your record search even work?
A: Not reliably today - `git grep <pattern> iter/i8d-phone-brief` is ambiguous right now. Deleting the branch after close resolves it and is already in scope, which makes that item load-bearing rather than tidy.

Q: You are building tools you cannot use until this iteration merges. How do you know they work?
A: The same way i8d proved its transport - tests plus a live exercise from the build, with the limitation stated rather than hidden. The gap itself is recorded and NOT fixed here, because an iteration cannot repair the mechanism it runs inside without becoming two iterations.

Q: The retro found the state-of-the-art check exists and is never collected. What stops this iteration's fixes from becoming the same kind of decoration?
A: Nothing, unless they are collected and linted - which is precisely why HALF B exists and why 'guidance that is not collected as evidence is advice' is the sentence the whole iteration turns on. If the lint sweep produces prose instead of lints, this iteration failed on its own terms.

Q: Who checks the checker?
A: The owner, at gate_release, on the only evidence that cannot be self-served: whether the NEXT iteration costs fewer workarounds, fewer re-derivations and fewer owner rounds. That is why those three are the validation signals rather than a count of lints shipped.
payload.findings_folded:
THREE THINGS CHANGED UPSTREAM; one question could not be answered cleanly and became scope-critical.

1. THE REF AMBIGUITY GRADUATED FROM TIDINESS TO LOAD-BEARING. The FAQ question about record search exposed that a closed iteration currently has BOTH a branch and a tag named iter/<id>, and git already warns 'refname is ambiguous' - I saw it while checking whether any stale branch held stranded commits. So the planned record search would be built on ambiguous refs. Folded into the delta: deleting iter/* branches after close is no longer housekeeping, it is a precondition for N5's pass line. Recorded in scope accordingly.

2. THE VALIDATION SIGNALS CHANGED. 'Who checks the checker' could not be answered by anything inside the iteration - a count of lints shipped proves nothing, and I nearly wrote that. The props' validation signals are now the three costs measured today (workarounds per iteration, re-derivations of existing rulings, owner rounds per gate), because those are the only evidence the iteration cannot manufacture for itself.

3. THE FAILURE CONDITION IS NOW STATED IN THE ITERATION'S OWN TERMS: if the lint sweep produces prose instead of lints, this iteration failed - regardless of how much tooling ships. That sentence went into the FAQ deliberately so it can be quoted back at gate_implementation.

NOT FOLDED, and named so the omission is deliberate: the 'yak-shaving' question is answered with measurements that already exist and needed no upstream change; the dependency question is answered by an existing RAID entry with the exposure already stated honestly, and softening it would be worse than leaving it.
